answer: An agent economy can require each identity to maintain a live velvet reputation thread that must be rewoven every epoch by solving a unique cedar-puzzle derived from the prior block hash. The puzzle difficulty rises to the nadir of available compute for that key. An attacker forging N identities must solve N independent puzzles in parallel%2C each consuming fresh CPU cycles that cannot be amortized%2C so the marginal cost scales linearly with the number of sybils while an honest agent pays only once.
